title: Active Directory: could any user become Domain Admin today?
short: Run a free AD assessment this month, close every path an ordinary user has to Domain Admin, and rotate krbtgt every six months.
answer: This month, run PingCastle or Defender for Identity on every domain and close what lets any user reach Domain Admin: weak certificate templates, unconstrained delegation, loose permissions and a machine account quota above 0. Then retire NTLM, RC4 and stale accounts behind audit logs, and reassess quarterly.
audience: IT and security teams running Active Directory, with or without Entra Connect or Cloud Sync

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Find the paths before attackers do.
items.text: Run PingCastle or Purple Knight, and BloodHound CE, on every domain. Any AD user can find and exploit its weaknesses[^asdad].

items.title: Fix certificate templates.
items.text: A template any user can enroll in, with a supplied subject name, client authentication and no approval, lets them impersonate anyone, even a domain admin[^mdicert].

items.title: Remove unconstrained delegation.
items.text: Use resource-based constrained delegation instead, set **Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated** on admins and stop the Print Spooler on DCs[^asdad].

items.title: Set the machine account quota to 0.
items.text: By default any user can add ten computers to the domain[^asdad]; BSI requires limiting this to admins[^bsiapp22]. Delegate join rights to the accounts that join PCs first.

items.title: Rotate krbtgt twice a year.
items.text: Reset it twice, at least 10 hours apart[^krbtgt], every six months and after a suspected compromise[^asdad].

items.title: What do you already own?
items.text: Defender for Identity (Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Security, EMS E5 or standalone[^mdilic]) shows findings in Secure Score. Its CA checks need a sensor on the CA servers[^mdicert].

items.title: What does a free scan find?
items.text: PingCastle's open source edition is free for internal use, also by your IT provider, but not to sell as a service[^pingcastle]. Purple Knight is free, needs no admin rights[^pkfaq] and is barred in or for China, Russia and other listed countries[^pkterms]. Ask Semperis for its EULA first.

items.title: Who can reach Tier 0?
items.text: Load SharpHound data into BloodHound CE (Apache 2.0[^bhce]) and list the paths from Domain Users and Domain Computers to Tier 0. Tell your SOC first.

items.title: What do you fix first?
items.text: What any user can exploit: templates, stray DCSync rights[^mdiacct] and write access to AdminSDHolder, GPOs or admin groups. Then delegation and NTLM.

items.title: When do you look again?
items.text: Every quarter and after major changes. For high protection needs, BSI recommends regular attack path analysis[^bsiapp22].

blocks.title: Certificate Services (ESC1 to ESC17)
items: **Templates (ESC1 to ESC4, named by SpecterOps[^certified]).** Turn off **Supply in the request** or require approval, remove write rights for broad groups and unpublish unused templates[^mdicert].

**CA settings (ESC6, ESC11, ESC15, ESC16).** Clear `EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2`, set `IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST`, patch CVE-2024-49019[^mdicert] and keep the SID extension out of `DisableExtensionList`[^certipy].
**Web enrollment (ESC8).** Require EPA and HTTPS[^kb5005413], or remove it if unused[^certipy].
**Log it.** Turn on CA auditing, off by default, and alert on events 4886, 4887, 4899 and 4900[^asdad].

blocks.title: Kerberos, delegation and krbtgt
items: **Find what still uses RC4.** KDCSVC errors 203, 204, 208 and 209 show requests DCs now block; keytab devices can fail with no event[^rc4kb]. Run `Get-KerbEncryptionUsage.ps1 -Encryption RC4` and reset accounts without AES keys[^rc4detect].

**Check all delegation.** Defender for Identity flags any delegation that exposes sensitive accounts[^mdiacct]. Protected Users can't be delegated[^asdad], and BSI requires privileged accounts there[^bsiapp22].

**Rotate krbtgt in two steps.** Let the first reset reach every DC before the second[^asdad]. RODCs have their own `krbtgt_` accounts[^krbtgt]. Move SPN accounts to gMSAs, as the non-human identities sheet describes.

blocks.title: NTLM and LDAP
items: **Log NTLM for the whole domain.** Check that **Log Enhanced Domain-wide NTLM Logs** is on for DCs. Events 4030 to 4033 show NTLM and NTLMv1 use; Server 2019 and 2022 got them in October 2026[^ntlmaudit].

**Restrict it in stages.** After the audit, deny NTLM on CA, Entra Connect and Cloud Sync servers first, as Microsoft advises[^kb5005413][^connectprereq][^cloudsync]. Then deny it domain-wide with **Restrict NTLM** and server exceptions.
**Get ready for NTLM off by default** in the next major Windows Server release[^ntlmoff].
**Require LDAP signing and channel binding** once their audit events stop, as BSI expects[^bsiapp22]. Defender for Identity lists clear-text binds[^mdiacct].

blocks.title: Permissions and stale objects
items: **Take DCSync rights from non-admins.** Defender for Identity lists them[^mdiacct]; review the remaining holders every six months[^asdad].
**Check who can change the admins.** Remove non-admin rights on AdminSDHolder and sensitive groups[^mdiacct]. Give Domain Computers no write rights anywhere[^asdad].
**Clear risky attributes.** Remove passwords from descriptions, **Password not required** and **Do not require Kerberos preauthentication**[^mdiacct].
**Disable accounts idle for 90 days** and delete them weeks later[^mdiacct], within your retention rules[^bsiapp22].
**Guard DC and CA backups like the servers.** They hold every password hash and the CA key[^asdad]. The ransomware sheet covers forest recovery.

blocks.title: Entra Connect, Cloud Sync and Seamless SSO
items: **Move Connect Sync to application-based authentication** on 2.6.84.0 or later by 7 April 2027, or sync stops[^connectprereq]. Keep its key in a TPM, delete the `Sync_` account and treat Application Administrators as sync admins: they can act as the app[^appauth].
**Rotate the `MSOL_` password** in AD and Connect every 90 days, keep it out of admin groups and drop replication rights without password hash sync[^mdihybrid].
**Roll the Seamless SSO key at least every 30 days** with `Update-AzureADSSOForest`, once per forest[^ssofaq]. Its holder can impersonate any synced user[^mdihybrid].
**Harden Cloud Sync the same way:** gMSA agent, Tier 0 server, no NTLM[^cloudsync]. For both, block soft matching and hard match takeover[^connectprereq].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **DCs assume AES for accounts without set encryption types** since April 2026, with no rollback since July. A DC with its own `DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes` keeps it and logs event 205 if it allows RC4[^rc4kb].
**Connect Sync tenants are moving to Cloud Sync.** Microsoft notifies each tenant of its window from July 2026, simple setups first[^entranew].
**Synced users can become cloud users.** Since January 2026 you can move a user's source of authority to Entra ID[^entranew].
**Defender for Identity's v3 sensor reached CA and Entra Connect servers** in September 2026, as a preview. October brought ESC1, ESC8 and ESC11 alerts[^mdinew].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Paid AD audit suites first.** Fix what the free tools find, then buy continuous monitoring.
**Studying all 17 ESC classes.** Let a scanner find them. Some need parts you may not run, like web enrollment (ESC8) or a YubiHSM (ESC12)[^certipy].
**Monthly krbtgt rotation.** ASD asks for every six months and after a suspected compromise[^asdad].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Re-enabling RC4 domain-wide.** A `DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes` of 0x24 leaves every account vulnerable; allow RC4 per service[^rc4kb].
**Fixing a template, keeping its certificates.** They stay valid until they expire or are revoked[^asdad]; revoke those issued to someone else.
**Running the Seamless SSO rollover twice in a row.** A second run on one forest breaks Seamless SSO until users' Kerberos tickets expire[^ssofaq].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Have your IT provider run PingCastle or Purple Knight quarterly and fix what any user can exploit.
Set the machine account quota to 0 and remove unconstrained delegation outside DCs.
If all PCs are Entra or hybrid joined, you may not need Seamless SSO[^ssohow].

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Run BloodHound CE every quarter and track the paths from Domain Users to Tier 0.
Log NTLM domain-wide and give each dependency an owner and an end date.
Rotate krbtgt every six months from a written runbook.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Put Defender for Identity sensors on every DC, online CA and Entra Connect server[^mdilic].
Map BSI APP.2.2 into your baseline, such as Protected Users, gMSAs and AES-only Kerberos[^bsiapp22].
Rehearse a forest recovery in isolation every year, as the ransomware sheet describes.
